text:
maria: Heads-up — started a canary enabling FP8 on H100 (TransformerEngine v2.4) for opt-30b. Seeing ~14% median throughput win but intermittent NaNs when KV replay hits long contexts (~6-10k tokens). Repro steps + small profiler excerpt below, cc @ajay @kevin :eyes:
ajay: Can you paste the kernel selection logs + TE config? Suspect a kernel fallback path mixing FP8/INT8 kernels across merged batches.
maria: Paste of relevant bits:
```
TE_CONFIG: {
  fp8_enabled: true,
  fp8_format: "e4m3",
  fp8_clip: 0.999,
  fallback_policy: "auto-mixed",
  batcher: { continuous: true, max_batch: 12, kv_merge: true }
}
KERNEL LOG excerpts:
[loader] selected kernel=te_fused_gemm_fp8_batched (lat 1.8ms)
[loader] fallback kernel=custom_matmul_int8 (lat 2.3ms)
[attention] detected NaN at step=342, kv_replay=true, merged_batch_id=87
PROFILER: tokens/sec=4200, p90_latency=48ms, p99=120ms
```
kevin: If kv_merge + continuous batching are merging requests with different calibration scales we can get out-of-range exponents. Try disabling kv_merge for the canary and reduce max_batch to 4. Also try fp8_clip=0.995 -> 0.98 to see sensitivity.
dana: Looks like calibration produced a couple of extreme per-channel scales on attention.qkv. Re-run calibration with per-channel histograms (not global), increase histogram bins to 2048, and use calib_clip=0.98 for a conservative run. We saw a similar pattern with L40S last sprint where one head had a 10x scale outlier.
perf-bot: Perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.example/reports/1849999999-fp8-h100 — median throughput +15%, NaN_rate=0.4% on canary set (last hour) :bar_chart:
sam: If that doesn't fix it, short-term mitigation: route problematic matmul ops to INT8 (matmul_fallback list) or enable mixed-precision fallback env var: TF_FP8_FALLBACK=1. That keeps the perf upside while avoiding rare instability.
ajay: Quick smoke: run ./scripts/smoke_fp8.sh --model opt-30b --seq 8192 --batch 8 --warmup 200 && tail -n 200 /var/log/runner.log. Also capture kernel-selection trace: export TE_TRACE=1; run.
maria: Ran a split test this morning. Findings:
- baseline canary (kv_merge=true, batch=8, fp8_clip=0.999): NaN_rate=0.38% across 3 runs, avg tokens/sec=4300
- changed to kv_merge=false, max_batch=4, per-layer calib (bins=2048), fp8_clip=0.999 -> NaN_rate dropped to 0% in 3/3 runs (10k tokens each), tokens/sec=4030 (~6.3% lower than FP8 baseline)
- enabling TF_FP8_FALLBACK=1 kept throughput similar to kv_merge=false case and stable.
So mitigation path: conservative per-layer calibration + disable kv_merge for now while we instrument scaling invariants.
kevin: Great. Add rollout guard: revert if NaN_rate > 0.1% or if kv_cache_hit_ratio drops >5%. Also add a metric 'kv_cache_scale_variance' so we can detect mixed-scale merges.
maria: Will open rollout PR with the conservative config and the guard thresholds. Also attaching raw logs to the PR. Link when ready. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary config applied to 2 h100 nodes (nodepool: fp8-canary-2)
maria: PR created: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/inference/+/fp8-h100-kv-stability — includes test harness, smoke script updates, and perf results. Will follow up with automation to run per-layer calib in CI.
